result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like signals and curb ramps are present, parked vehicles near the crossing create sightline obstructions for pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked vans on the left side of the street near the crosswalk block the sight lines between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, just before the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines.

result.summary: The image depicts a signalized urban intersection featuring high-visibility continental crosswalks and wide, well-maintained sidewalks. While pedestrian signals and 'No Turn on Red' signage enhance safety, the multi-lane one-way configuration creates a wide crossing distance that increases pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Multi-lane crossing exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple travel and parking lanes, increasing the time spent in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground crosswalk spanning the width of the street

result.summary: The image depicts a signalized urban intersection on a one-way street with high-visibility continental crosswalks and well-maintained sidewalks. hazards.name: Potential for high vehicle speeds
hazards.description: The wide, one-way street layout without physical traffic calming may encourage higher vehicle speeds through the intersection.
